newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Brazil supreme court set to vote Wed on CVRD sale.
newsitem.headline: Brazil supreme court set to vote Wed on CVRD sale.

text.p: Brazil's highest court would probably rule Wednesday on whether the upcoming privatization of mining giant Companhia Vale do Rio Doce, is constitutional, an official said.

The Supreme Federal Tribunal (STF) was due to rule on two actions brought by the Order of Brazilian Lawyers, a private lawyers group, which has questioned aspects of the CVRD selloff, an STF spokesman said.
Left-wing political parties have also sought an STF injunction against the privatization due to begin April 29 with the sale of 40-45 percent of CVRD's voting capital.
The parties' case may also be heard Wednesday, the spokesman said.
About 70 challenges to the CVRD privatization are reported to have been lodged in court across Brazil, raising the possibilty of a delay in the sale timetable.

"There has so far not been any decision taken that would lead to a delay. But the auction could easily be rescheduled for the week after April 29 should there be a need," said a spokeswoman for Planning Minister Antonio Kandir.

Newspapers Monday quoted Jose Pio Borges, the National Development Bank's privatization director, as saying the April 29 auction might be postponed given the sheer number of court cases lodged against it.
Most of the legal challenges focus on the transfer of CVRD's mineral rights to the private sector once the company is sold.
Opponents of the sale say that would contravene an article of the consitutution, which says Brazil's mineral wealth belongs to the Brazilian state.
The government argue the new owners of CVRD will not actually own the mineral rights, but instead would be offered concessions to exploit them.
